text:
sara: Quick heads-up — canary for runtime v2.4.0 is showing a latency regression vs baseline. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~220ms on long-context workloads. requesting a quick gate check. :warning:
ben: saw that in the dashboard too. is it across all models or just the llama-kv profile?
leila: looks concentrated on llama-kv + seq>2048, likely KV cache eviction pattern. i have flame graphs but need a minute to upload.
ops-bot: Canary hold triggered by perf-gate (p95 > 170ms) at 2026-03-17T09:23:12Z
mike: @sara can you paste the raw numbers? throughput, error rate, and which region?
sara: sure — staging canary (us-west-2): baseline p95=120ms, canary p95=220ms, token throughput -18%, errors steady at 0.2% (unchanged). load profile was identical: 95th percentile seq=2600 samples
ben: thanks. does the profiler show more memcpy/GPU to CPU transfers? that would explain the jump.
leila: uploading flame: https://redwood.internal/prof/trace-7f3a (link valid for 24h). main hotspot is cache compact + allocator churn during attention KV rebuild.
mike: that matches an allocator change in 2.4.0 — we switched to the new slab allocator for small KV segments. reverting allocator might be fastest rollback.
sara: can we do a targeted revert just for the allocator? patch would be `ENV_KV_ALLOC=legacy` and restart canary pods. low-risk if config only.
josh: decision needed: do we hold + rollback canary to v2.3.9, or flip the config flag? pros/cons?
ben: config flip is quick and reversible. but config may mask underlying bug that could resurface. rollback gives more time for a proper fix.
leila: we can flip config now (5m) and simultaneously prepare a rollback artifact. i can run a quick sanity perf run after flipping.
mike: i'm +1 for config flip now, then rollback if no improvement in 10m. we should notify customers if we escalate.
sara: doing the flip now: `kubectl set env deployment/runtime-canary ENV_KV_ALLOC=legacy -n canary`
ops-bot: Command executed: set env on deployment/runtime-canary by sara at 09:26:03Z
leila: running perf probe — will post numbers in ~6m.
ben: also kick off the diff traces: `./tools/trace-collector --canary` to capture end-to-end.
leila: quick update: p95 dropped to 130ms after flag flip, throughput back within 4% of baseline. looks promising.
josh: good. do we keep canary running with flag or rollback to stable? risk tolerance?
mike: keep canary with flag for now, but gate the release. open a ticket to revert allocator change and add unit tests for KV compaction.
sara: filed INF-1288 with reproducer + flame link. tagging @eng-ml for follow-up.
ben: one more ask — add an automated smoke test for seq>2048 in canary pipeline.
josh: agreed. i'll mark the canary as "flagged" (not promoted) and schedule a rollback window if fix not in by EOD. everyone okay?
mike: ack
leila: ack
ben: ack
ops-bot: Canary status: FLAGGED (manual hold) — awaiting follow-up. Logged at 2026-03-17T09:33:09Z
josh: thanks team. i'll update the release board and close this thread once we have a remediation plan. :white_check_mark:
